patch: 0782-perf-spec-decode-copy-drafter-survival-and-tile-cap.patch (the selection's context-only rebase of the PR's 0762; SHA-256 f56bd1a2...)
mark: Its screen_copy_drafter_smooth.py 58-layer step screen on the image, 2 boots: the single-stream initial copy step and the post-reject shrunk step faster beyond the interval at TP3; paired decode at 1 stream better and at 8 streams not worse; temperature-0 text unchanged
evidence: The PR's screen_copy_drafter_smooth.py from its head, unmodified (--boot boot1/boot2, -w /opt/spark-ds41f/candidate/vllm), on the candidate arm twice. It compares two hand-chosen step shapes in-process; its 'parent' policy is simulated (single_req_tile_spill_scale = 0.55, dead_rows_tau = 0.0). On the base arm it stops at its first assert (copy_apply admits no 2-token copy there): script-base-boot1.txt, recorded once.

Policy-driven image A/B (harness ab971.py, ABBA, same session, -e SPARK_DS41F_DSPARK_DEAD_ROWS_TAU=0.2 as config/cluster.json sets it for every shape): each image's own copy_apply kernel and AdaptiveVerificationManager (built as the PR's make_manager builds it) decide the c1 initial copy step (0.95 prior, row_cost 0.035) and the post-reject shrunk step (5 live drafts, -1 tail at confidence 0) through the image's dead_row_args and combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens, at two dead-row taus: 'recipe' (the module's _DEAD_ROWS_TAU = 0.2) and 'pr' (0.0, the PR's make_manager). The PR's 58-layer step workload (one routed MoE layer + one dense GEMM per graph replay, x58) then times each image's chosen shape; 50 warm-up replays (>100 ms) and 40 timed, warm and 128 MiB wash, TP3 and TP4. All four shapes are timed on both images, which gives an A/A floor (identical kernels).
The PR's tests on the candidate arm, twice, -v --noconftest.

measured.pr_script_candidate_image: Reproduces the PR in-process: TP3 initial step 158.0/152.9 -> 151.3/146.4 ms (warm, boot1/boot2), shrunk step 156.4/157.4 -> 62.5/61.0 ms; TP4 initial 118.5/118.4 -> 112.6/111.7, shrunk 116.1/119.4 -> 44.5/44.8. Gates: candidate admits 2/3/4/8-token copies, c1 16 tokens (16-row graph), shrunk step 6 unmasked rows, dead cut 5.

shrunk_step_tau_recipe_0.2.candidate: the same cut, 6 unmasked rows in a 16-row graph

shrunk_step_tau_0.base: dead_row_args None, 17 unmasked rows in a 24-row graph
shrunk_step_tau_0.candidate: log_tau -1e30, cut 5, 6 unmasked rows in a 16-row graph

pytest_candidate.note: PR receipt 108 passed, 1 skipped; the candidate's files carry other patches' tests

parts.part: single-stream initial copy step faster beyond the interval at TP3
parts.detail: serving tau (0.2): TP3 -5.1% warm (155.6/157.5 -> 149.0/148.2 ms), -5.3% wash; TP4 -4.2%/-5.5%; all beyond the interval. The tile cap moves the step from the 24-row to the 16-row graph.

parts.part: post-reject shrunk step faster beyond the interval at TP3
parts.detail: On the serving path (SPARK_DS41F_DSPARK_DEAD_ROWS_TAU=0.2, set for every shape in config/cluster.json) the base already marks the -1 tail as dead rows (6 unmasked rows): TP3 -0.95% warm, -0.3% wash, same within the interval (TP4 -1.2%/-4.4%, same). The PR's -60% exists only at tau 0 (reproduced: -60.6%/-59.4% at TP3), which the recipe does not run; its README calls tau 0 'the promoted default'. The patch's dead-row change (log_tau -1e30 when tau <= 0, dead_rows declared for the copy drafter) is inert at the recipe's tau.

no cell of the policy-driven A/B is worse. The A/A floor (identical kernels timed on both images) is a median |change| of 0.5% (range 0.05-4.5%, the largest from boot outliers); two A/A cells flag 'worse' under the cell rule, at +0.7% and +1.9%, which is noise of identical code

parts.part: paired decode at 1 stream better, at 8 streams not worse; temperature-0 text unchanged
parts.detail: multi-node: the coordinator's tp3-switched screen with its single-stream and sampled companions, and the determinism gate

verdict_scope: sp8-evaluable parts; paired decode and temperature-0 text are the tp3-switched screen's and gate's
reason: The mark declares two faster cells at TP3. The tile cap gives the first on the serving path (-5.1%/-5.3% on the c1 initial copy step, beyond the interval). The second, the post-reject shrunk step's -60%, does not occur on the path serving takes: the recipe's dead-row tau of 0.2 already masks the trailing -1 rows in the base, so the shrunk step is the same within the interval (-0.3% to -0.95% at TP3); the PR measured it at tau 0. No cell is slower.
rework_hint: Re-declare the mark on the tile cap and the copy_apply survival gate (the parts that act at tau 0.2), or drop the inert tau-0 dead-row change; the 1-stream paired decode row decides the tile cap's serving value.
notes: copy_apply's survival yield is confirmed on the image: 2- and 3-token copies are now admitted against DSpark's [0.70..0.50] confidences (base: not admitted). Its effect on decode is a drafting change the screen's single-stream and sampled companions measure.
Same-shape A/A: the four step shapes timed on both images with identical kernels differ by -3.5% to +4.5% (TP4 24x6 warm has a 4.8 ms outlier boot on c53 boot2, TP4 24x6 wash one on base boot2).
